name: Cmd
doc:
A simple framework for writing line-oriented command interpreters.

These are often useful for test harnesses, administrative tools, and
prototypes that will later be wrapped in a more sophisticated interface.

A Cmd instance or subclass instance is a line-oriented interpreter
framework.  There is no good reason to instantiate Cmd itself; rather,
it's useful as a superclass of an interpreter class you define yourself
in order to inherit Cmd's methods and encapsulate action methods.

changed.text: completekey='tab' is replaced by '^I' for editline.

name: cmdloop
doc:
Repeatedly issue a prompt, accept input, parse an initial prefix
off the received input, and dispatch to action methods, passing them
the remainder of the line as argument.

name: cmdqueue
doc: A list of queued input lines. The cmdqueue list is checked in cmdloop() when new input is needed; if it is nonempty, its elements will be processed in order, as if entered at the prompt.

name: columnize
doc:
Display a list of strings as a compact set of columns.

Each column is only as wide as necessary.
Columns are separated by two spaces (one was not legible enough).

name: completedefault
doc:
Method called to complete an input line when no command-specific
complete_*() method is available.

By default, it returns an empty list.

name: default
doc:
Called on an input line when the command prefix is not recognized.

If this method is not overridden, it prints an error message and
returns.

name: do_help
doc: List available commands with "help" or detailed help with "help cmd".

name: doc_header
doc: The header to issue if the help output has a section for documented commands.

name: emptyline
doc:
Called when an empty line is entered in response to the prompt.

If this method is not overridden, it repeats the last nonempty
command entered.

name: identchars
doc: The string of characters accepted for the command prefix.

name: intro
doc: A string to issue as an intro or banner. May be overridden by giving the cmdloop() method an argument.

name: lastcmd
doc: The last nonempty command prefix seen.

name: misc_header
doc: The header to issue if the help output has a section for miscellaneous help topics (that is, there are help_*() methods without corresponding do_*() methods).

name: onecmd
doc:
Interpret the argument as though it had been typed in response
to the prompt.

This may be overridden, but should not normally need to be;
see the precmd() and postcmd() methods for useful execution hooks.
The return value is a flag indicating whether interpretation of
commands by the interpreter should stop.

name: postcmd
doc: Hook method executed just after a command dispatch is finished.

name: postloop
doc:
Hook method executed once when the cmdloop() method is about to
return.

name: precmd
doc:
Hook method executed just before the command line is
interpreted, but after the input prompt is generated and issued.

name: preloop
doc: Hook method executed once when the cmdloop() method is called.

name: prompt
doc: The prompt issued to solicit input.

name: ruler
doc: The character used to draw separator lines under the help-message headers. If empty, no ruler line is drawn. It defaults to '='.

name: undoc_header
doc: The header to issue if the help output has a section for undocumented commands (that is, there are do_*() methods without corresponding help_*() methods).

name: use_rawinput
doc: A flag, defaulting to true. If true, cmdloop() uses input() to display a prompt and read the next command; if false, sys.stdout.write() and sys.stdin.readline() are used. (This means that by importing readline, on systems that support it, the interpreter will automatically support Emacs-like line editing and command-history keystrokes.)
